Python: training

Source: vignettes/articles/python-training.Rmd
python-training.Rmd

Fitting a model, cross-validating it and pretraining its encoder without labels: the model and its architecture settings, the trainer and its settings, what a fit returns, the held-out evaluations, and the pretrainers.

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

The examples on this page run in order on the survey that ships with the R package: 150 plots in the Alps, with one table of plots and one of the species recorded on them. Training and reading the fit walks through the same steps with their output.

ResolveModel 

ResolveModel(schema, config=ModelConfig())

The network: a species encoder, a shared encoder that turns a plot’s inputs into its latent representation (a vector of latent_dim numbers), and one output head per target. The schema fixes the input widths and the heads. The encoding settings that also size the model (the species encoding, hash_dim, top_k, top_k_species and the taxonomy slot count) come from the dataset’s loader settings through model_config_for_dataset.

import os
import tempfile

import pandas as pd
import torch
import resolve_core as rc

data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcol33/resolve/master/r/inst/extdata/"
plots = pd.read_csv(data + "plots.csv")
species = pd.read_csv(data + "species.csv")

roles = rc.RoleMapping()
roles.plot_id = "plot_id"
roles.species_id = "species"
roles.abundance = "cover"
roles.genus = "genus"
roles.family = "family"
roles.latitude = "lat"
roles.longitude = "lon"
targets = [rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation"),
           rc.TargetSpec.classification("habitat", 4)]
dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets)

model_config = rc.ModelConfig()
model_config.hidden_dims = [128, 64]
model = rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema,
                        rc.model_config_for_dataset(dataset, model_config))
model.latent_dim

Forward passes 

forward(continuous, genus_ids=None, family_ids=None, species_ids=None,
        species_vector=None, pool_genus_ids=None, pool_family_ids=None,
        pool_weights=None, pool_mask=None, pool_has_cover=None,
        categorical_ids=None)

The model’s outputs for a batch of plots, one tensor per target: a regression target in standardised units, a classification target as logits. continuous is the continuous block (ResolveDataset.continuous_block), standardised; the other inputs are the dataset tensors of the same names, and the encoding decides which are needed. A model with categorical columns given no categorical_ids reads every one as unknown. Calling the model, model(...), is the same as forward.

The other forward methods take the same inputs, positionally in this order or by keyword:

  • get_latent(...): the latent representation, (batch, latent_dim).
  • forward_with_aux(...): a ModelForwardResult, the outputs with the auxiliary loss terms.
  • forward_single(target, ...): the output of one target’s head.
  • encode_with_activations(...): the latent and a list with the activations of every hidden layer of the species encoder’s final stage, each (rows, neurons); empty for the tabular architectures and TraitNet.
  • get_gate_probs(...): the mixture-of-experts gate probabilities, (batch, n_experts); None without a mixture.
inputs = dict(genus_ids=dataset.genus_ids, family_ids=dataset.family_ids)
model.eval()
outputs = model(dataset.continuous_block(True), **inputs)
{name: out.shape for name, out in outputs.items()}

Attributes

  • schema (ResolveSchema) and config (ModelConfig): what the model was built from.
  • latent_dim (int): the width of the latent representation.
  • species_encoding (SpeciesEncodingMode) and uses_explicit_vector (bool): the species encoder, and whether it reads species_vector.
  • uses_moe (bool) and n_experts (int): whether a mixture of experts routes the plots, and over how many experts.
  • aux_loss_names (list[str]): the auxiliary loss terms the model reports: moe with a mixture of experts, tabnet_sparsity for TabNet.
  • row_reference_rows (int): the training rows SAINT’s row attention keeps as the reference set inference attends over; 0 for other architectures.
  • requires_species_graph, has_species_graph (bool), species_graph_edge_index and species_graph_edge_type: the species graph of a heterogeneous GNN.

Methods

  • parameters() (list[Tensor], ready for a torch optimiser), named_parameters() (dict), state_dict() (dict of cloned parameters and buffers), load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=True) (returns the missing and the unexpected keys) and n_parameters().
  • train(mode=True), eval(), zero_grad(), requires_grad_(requires_grad=True) and to(device), where device is "cpu", "cuda" or "cuda:N".
  • get_species_weights(), get_genus_weights(), get_family_weights(): the embedding tables, (n_species_vocab, species_embed_dim) and the like, or None where the encoding has no such table.
  • composition_parameters(): the species, genus and family tables the species encoder reads a plot’s composition through, as the parameters themselves.
  • set_traits(traits): attach the species trait matrix of the TraitNet architecture; the model keeps it in a buffer and saves it in the checkpoint.
  • set_species_graph(edge_index, edge_type): replace the species graph of a heterogeneous GNN (see build_species_graph).

ModelForwardResult

What forward_with_aux returns: outputs (dict[str, Tensor], one entry per target) and aux_losses (dict[str, Tensor]), the auxiliary terms the forward adds to the training loss, each already weighted: moe (the mixture-of-experts load balancing, times moe_aux_loss_weight) and tabnet_sparsity (TabNet’s mask entropy, times tabnet.sparsity_coefficient). Empty for a model with neither.

model_config_for_dataset() 

model_config_for_dataset(dataset, config=ModelConfig())

config with the fields that size a model to its data taken from dataset: species_encoding, hash_dim, top_k and top_k_species from its loader settings, and n_taxonomy_slots from the width of its genus slots. Build a model for a dataset as ResolveModel(dataset.schema, model_config_for_dataset(dataset, config)).

ModelConfig 

ModelConfig()

The architecture of a model.

model_config = rc.ModelConfig()
model_config.hidden_dims = [256, 128, 64]
model_config.dropout = 0.2
model_config.activation = rc.ActivationType.SiLU

Species encoding:

  • species_encoding (SpeciesEncodingMode, default Hash), hash_dim (int, default 32), top_k (int, default 3), top_k_species (int, default 10): as on the dataset; model_config_for_dataset copies them.
  • n_taxonomy_slots (int, default 3): the genus and family slots per plot, twice top_k under TopBottom.
  • uses_explicit_vector (bool, default False): read the sparse species vector, which turns Hash into Sparse; refused with Embed, RankPool and Transformer.
  • species_embed_dim (int, default 32), genus_emb_dim and family_emb_dim (int, default 8), categorical_embed_dim (int, default 8): embedding widths.

Shared encoder:

  • hidden_dims (list[int], default [2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64]): the layer widths; the last is the latent width.
  • dropout (float, default 0.3), activation (ActivationType, default GELU), normalization (NormLayerType, default BatchNorm), norm_groups (int, default 32, for GroupNorm), use_residual (bool, default False), leaky_relu_slope (float, default 0.01), elu_alpha (float, default 1.0).

Heads:

  • head_hidden_dims (list[int], default [], one linear layer per target), head_activation (ActivationType, default GELU), head_dropout (float, default 0.0).

Pooled and transformer encodings:

  • cover_dropout (float, default 0.0): the probability of replacing a plot’s pool weights with its presence mask during training.
  • plot_totals (bool, default False): add each plot’s combined cover and log(1 + species count) to the pooled features, with a flag saying they are present.
  • plot_totals_dropout (float, default 0.0): with plot_totals, the probability of withholding a training plot’s totals, so the model also predicts without them (Predictor.plot_totals = False).
  • freeze_composition (bool, default False): keep the species, genus and family tables at their initial values. Needs the MLP architecture and an encoding with such a table.
  • d_model (int, default 128), n_heads (int, default 4), n_attention_layers (int, default 0, pooling alone), transformer_ff_dim (int, default 256), transformer_dropout (float, default 0.1), transformer_pooling (TransformerPooling, default Attention).

Mixture of experts:

  • moe_routing (MoERoutingType, default None_): no mixture, Soft or TopK routing.
  • moe_placement (MoEPlacement, default Tail), n_experts (int, default 4, at least 2), expert_hidden_dims (list[int], default [256, 128]), moe_top_k (int, default 2), moe_noise_std (float, default 0.1, routing noise during training), moe_aux_loss_weight (float, default 0.01, the weight of the load-balancing loss).

Architecture:

  • encoder_architecture (EncoderArchitecture, default MLP): replaces the shared MLP; each architecture reads its settings from its own sub-configuration: ft_transformer, tabnet, saint, excelformer, trait_net, gnn, heterogeneous_gnn.
  • parallel_layers (ParallelLayersConfig) and tabm (TabMConfig): alternative final stages of the MLP encoder.

The final stage of the MLP encoder is one of four: the plain MLP, a tail-placed mixture of experts, TabM, or a block of parallel branches. At most one of the last three may be enabled; moe_placement = MoEPlacement.Post moves the mixture after the encoder, where it combines with either of the others.

Every species encoding reaches the tabular architectures as numeric features beside the continuous block, and the genus and family slots of Hash, Embed and Sparse as categorical inputs. HeterogeneousGNN and the CoOccurrence GNN graph read the species vector and need Sparse; the Taxonomic GNN graph reads the genus and family slots and does not take RankPool or Transformer. Building the model refuses an unsupported pair with a message naming what would work.

FTTransformerConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.FTTransformer, ModelConfig.ft_transformer: a transformer over one token per input feature. d_model (192), n_heads (8), n_layers (3), attention_dropout (0.2, on the attention weights), ffn_dropout (0.1, inside the feed-forward layer and on each sublayer’s residual branch), ffn_multiplier (4) and pre_norm (True).

TabNetConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.TabNet, ModelConfig.tabnet: n_steps (3), n_d and n_a (64), relaxation_factor (1.5), sparsity_coefficient (0.001), virtual_batch_size (128) and use_sparsemax (True). use_sparsemax = False selects 1.5-entmax (Peters, Niculae and Martins 2019), which keeps more features per step than sparsemax. virtual_batch_size is the slice ghost batch normalisation runs at; 0 normalises the batch in one piece. TabNet adds sparsity_coefficient times the entropy of its feature masks to the training loss, recorded as tabnet_sparsity.

SAINTConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.SAINT, ModelConfig.saint: d_model (128), n_heads (8), n_layers (6), attention_dropout (0.1), use_row_attention (True) and row_attention_rows (256). SAINT attends across rows as well as features. In training a batch is cut into groups of row_attention_rows rows; at inference each plot attends over a fixed reference set of row_attention_rows - 1 training rows plus itself, saved with the weights, so a plot’s prediction does not depend on which plots share its batch.

ExcelFormerConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.ExcelFormer, ModelConfig.excelformer: d_model (192), n_heads (8), n_layers (3), attention_dropout (0.2), ffn_multiplier (4), importance_threshold (0.5) and pre_norm (True).

GNNConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.GNN, ModelConfig.gnn: a graph neural network over a k-nearest-neighbour graph of the plots in a forward pass. gnn_type (GNNType, GAT), n_layers (3), hidden_dim (256), n_heads (4), k_neighbors (10), graph_mode (GraphConstructionMode, Spatial), edge_dropout (0.1) and use_edge_features (False). graph_mode is what neighbourhood is measured on: the coordinates, the genus and family composition, or the species vector. A spatial graph trains on the whole training set in one batch, so the graph spans every plot. use_edge_features weights each edge by its similarity instead of 1.

HeterogeneousGNNConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.HeterogeneousGNN, ModelConfig.heterogeneous_gnn: message passing on a graph over the species vocabulary (build_species_graph). hidden_dim (128), output_dim (64), n_layers (3), n_edge_types (3), n_heads (4), dropout (0.1), k_cooccurrence (20), cooccurrence_threshold (0.01), use_taxonomic_edges (True) and use_cooccurrence_edges (True). Trainer.prepare_data builds the graph from the dataset and the checkpoint carries it.

TraitNetConfig

The settings of EncoderArchitecture.TraitNet, ModelConfig.trait_net: env_dim (128), trait_dim (64), interaction_dim (256), interaction (TraitInteractionMode, Bilinear) and shared_trait_encoder (True). interaction is how the environment and a species’ traits combine and interaction_dim the width of the result; shared_trait_encoder = False gives every species its own trait encoder. The trait matrix comes in through ResolveModel.set_traits.

TabMConfig

TabM, an ensemble of MLPs sharing most of their weights, as the encoder’s final stage, ModelConfig.tabm: enabled (False), n_ensembles (16) and aggregation (TabMAggregation, Mean).

ParallelLayersConfig

A block of parallel branches as the encoder’s final stage, ModelConfig.parallel_layers: enabled (False), branches (list[ParallelBranchConfig]), aggregation (ParallelAggregation, Concat), attention_heads (4) and use_residual (True). Enabled, the block replaces the plain MLP, so the branches carry the encoder’s final capacity.

ParallelBranchConfig

One branch of a parallel block: hidden_dims ([]), activation (GELU), normalization (BatchNorm), dropout (0.3) and branch_weight (1.0), the factor on the branch’s output in the aggregation; 0 takes it out of the sum and keeps its parameters.

branch = rc.ParallelBranchConfig()
branch.hidden_dims = [64, 32]
parallel = rc.ModelConfig()
parallel.parallel_layers.enabled = True
parallel.parallel_layers.branches = [branch, branch]

Trainer 

Trainer(model, config)

Fits a model: it holds the split into fitting and held-out plots, the optimiser, the training loop and the evaluations on the held-out plots.

config = rc.TrainConfig()
config.max_epochs = 100
trainer = rc.Trainer(model, config)
trainer.prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42)
result = trainer.fit()
result.final_metrics["elevation"]["mae"]

prepare_data() 

prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42)
prepare_data(dataset, stopping_indices, seed=42)

Splits the plots, fits the input and target scalers on the fitting plots, and records the categorical codes. The held-out fold is the set of plots training does not fit on: early stopping, the best epoch, the final metrics and the evaluations read them. The first form holds out a random test_size share of the plots, drawn with seed; test_size=0 holds out nothing and needs fixed_epochs. The second holds out the plots at the positions stopping_indices (from ResolveDataset.plot_indices), such as a spatial block; seed then orders the fitting plots and seeds the epoch shuffle.

Each call replaces everything an earlier one set. prepare_data raises when the dataset and model hash widths disagree, when the split leaves no plot to fit, and, for an explicit fold, for an empty fold, a position out of range or listed twice, a fold of every plot, and a fold with no labelled plot for a target whose missing policy is Mask. For a heterogeneous GNN it also builds the species graph.

seed fixes the split. The starting weights come from torch’s global random number generator when the model is built, so seed that generator before building the model to repeat a fit.

fold = dataset.plot_indices(["A001", "A002", "A003", "A004", "A005"])
trainer.prepare_data(dataset, stopping_indices=fold, seed=42)
trainer.test_plot_ids()

prepare_data_raw(*, targets, coordinates=None, covariates=None, ..., categorical_ids=None, test_size=0.2, seed=42) takes the inputs as tensors by keyword instead: the parts of the continuous block and the other model inputs as in Predictor.predict, and targets, a dict of target name to (n_plots,) tensor.

fit() 

fit()

Trains and returns a TrainResult. The run stops at max_epochs, or earlier once patience epochs pass without improvement on the held-out fold, and keeps the weights of the best epoch. With fixed_epochs it runs that many epochs of the max_epochs schedule and keeps the final weights. On a CUDA out-of-memory error it halves batch_size and restarts, down to batch_size_floor; effective_batch_size is the batch size it trained at. The held-out fold is scored in chunks; an out-of-memory error there halves the chunk.

resume() 

resume(checkpoint_path)

Continues a run from a checkpoint fit wrote while training, best.pt or checkpoint_<N>.pt under TrainConfig.checkpoint_dir, at the epoch after it, with its optimiser, early-stopping, mixed-precision and random-number state, and returns the result of the whole run. The trainer needs the run’s model architecture and settings (Trainer.load_train_config) and must be prepared on the run’s data with its seed. Raises ValueError for a checkpoint without run progress or a split that differs from the run’s.

run_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
config = rc.TrainConfig()
config.max_epochs = 60
config.fixed_epochs = 60
config.checkpoint_dir = run_dir
config.checkpoint_every = 20
run = rc.Trainer(rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, model.config), config)
run.prepare_data(dataset, seed=42)
run.fit()

again = rc.Trainer(rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, model.config),
                   rc.Trainer.load_train_config(
                       os.path.join(run_dir, "checkpoint_40.pt")))
again.prepare_data(dataset, seed=42)
resumed = again.resume(os.path.join(run_dir, "checkpoint_40.pt"))
resumed.resumed_from_epoch

Evaluations of the held-out fold

  • compute_residuals(target_name): a ResidualAnalysis of a regression target.
  • compute_classification_predictions(target_name): a ClassificationPredictions of a classification target.
  • compute_calibration(target_name, n_bins=10): a CalibrationResult of a classification target; no bins for a regression target.
  • compute_diagnostics(): a NetworkDiagnostics of the species encoder’s final stage, under every species encoding; not for the tabular architectures or TraitNet.
  • test_plot_ids(), train_plot_ids(): the plot identifiers of the held-out and the fitting plots, after prepare_data(dataset); test_indices(), train_indices(): their positions in the dataset, as int64 tensors.
trainer.prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42)
result = trainer.fit()
residuals = trainer.compute_residuals("elevation")
classes = trainer.compute_classification_predictions("habitat")
calibration = trainer.compute_calibration("habitat", n_bins=5)
calibration.expected_calibration_error

cross_validate() 

cross_validate(n_folds=5, seed=42)
cross_validate_spatial(spatial_config, n_folds=5, seed=42)

Cross-validation fits the model once per fold, each time holding out one of n_folds parts of the plots, and scores each fit on the part it held out. cross_validate draws the folds at random with seed; cross_validate_spatial cuts the plots into blocks of latitude and longitude (SpatialBlockConfig) and assigns whole blocks to folds, so a fold’s plots lie apart from the plots it was fitted on. Both return a CrossValidationResult, start each fold from the model’s initial weights, and restore the trainer’s own split when they finish. Spatial blocks need coordinates, and fewer blocks than folds is an error.

folds = trainer.cross_validate(n_folds=3, seed=1)
blocks = rc.SpatialBlockConfig()
blocks.lat_size = 0.5
blocks.lon_size = 0.5
spatial = trainer.cross_validate_spatial(blocks, n_folds=3, seed=1)
spatial.mean_metrics["elevation"]["mae"]

predict() 

predict(continuous, genus_ids=None, family_ids=None, ...)

The model’s outputs in evaluation mode, from the unstandardised continuous block, standardised here with the fitted scalers, and the other inputs of ResolveModel.forward: a regression target in its original units, a classification target as logits. For a whole dataset, save a checkpoint and use Predictor.

Checkpoints 

save(path, metadata=None)
load_state(path, device="cpu", vram_fraction=1.0)
Trainer.load(path, device="cpu", vram_fraction=1.0)
Trainer.load_train_config(path)
Trainer.load_run_metadata(path)

save writes the model, the scalers and the vocabularies to a checkpoint, with the run’s RunMetadata when metadata is given (trainer.run_metadata). load_state loads a checkpoint’s weights, scalers and categorical codes into this trainer, which then evaluates as the original run did when it is built and prepared the same way; a missing parameter or buffer raises. The static load returns the model, its Scalers and its CategoricalVocab. load_train_config returns the TrainConfig the checkpoint records; settings it does not record (device, checkpoint directory, mixed-precision and cuDNN flags) keep their defaults. load_run_metadata returns its RunMetadata. A file that cannot be read or written raises StorageError.

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "model.pt")
trainer.save(path, metadata=trainer.run_metadata)
rc.Trainer.load_run_metadata(path).n_plots_train

Attributes

  • model (ResolveModel) and config (TrainConfig).
  • scalers (Scalers): the scaling fitted on the fitting plots.
  • categorical_vocab (CategoricalVocab): the categorical codes recorded by prepare_data.
  • run_metadata (RunMetadata): the split prepare_data made and, after fit, the run’s timing, epochs and final metrics.
  • effective_batch_size (int): the batch size the last fit trained at; 0 before the first.

TrainConfig 

TrainConfig()

The settings of a training run.

Run length and selection:

  • max_epochs (int, default 500), patience (int, default 50): the epoch limit, and the epochs without improvement that stop the run.
  • fixed_epochs (int, default 0): run this many epochs of the max_epochs schedule and keep the final weights; 0 stops early.
  • selection_metric (SelectionMetric, default Loss): the held-out value early stopping, the best epoch and ReduceOnPlateau follow.
  • batch_size (int, default 4096), batch_size_floor (int, default 1024): the plots per optimiser step, and the smallest batch the out-of-memory retry drops to.

Optimiser and learning rate:

  • lr (float, default 0.001), weight_decay (float, default 0.0001): the AdamW learning rate and weight decay.
  • lr_scheduler (LRSchedulerType, default None_): how the rate changes over the run.
  • lr_step_size (int, default 100), lr_gamma (float, default 0.1): the period and factor of StepLR.
  • lr_min (float, default 1e-6): the end point of CosineAnnealing and LinearDecay, and the floor of ReduceOnPlateau.
  • lr_plateau_factor (float, default 0.1), lr_plateau_patience (int, default 10), lr_plateau_threshold (float, default 0.0), lr_plateau_cooldown (int, default 0): ReduceOnPlateau, PyTorch’s ReduceLROnPlateau on the held-out value selection_metric names. With threshold 0 it counts improvement by early stopping’s rule.
  • warmup_steps (int, default 0) or warmup_epochs (int, default 0), not both: a linear warmup over that many optimiser steps or epochs, which scales every schedule.

Loss:

  • loss_config (LossConfigMode, default Combined): the regression loss.
  • phase_boundaries ((int, int), default (100, 300)): the epochs at which the Combined regression loss changes phase: mean absolute error, then with the symmetric mean absolute percentage error added, then with a penalty outside the tolerance band added.
  • band_threshold (float, default 0.25): the tolerance band of that penalty. band_thresholds (list[float], default [0.1, 0.25, 0.5]): the relative bands with a reported accuracy (band_10, band_25, band_50).
  • nca_temperature (float, default 0.1), nca_neighbors (int, default 32), nca_weight (float, default 0.1): the neighbourhood components analysis term of LossConfigMode.NCA.

Device and precision:

  • device (str, default "cpu"): "cpu", "cuda" or "cuda:N".
  • use_amp (bool, default False): mixed precision on CUDA, with amp_init_scale (65536.0), amp_growth_factor (2.0), amp_backoff_factor (0.5) and amp_growth_interval (2000) for the gradient scale.
  • cudnn_benchmark (bool, default True), allow_tf32 (bool, default True), vram_fraction (float, default 1.0, the share of GPU memory the run may use).

Checkpoints:

  • checkpoint_dir (str, default ""): the directory for best.pt, checkpoint_<N>.pt, progress.json and the final checkpoint.pt; empty writes none.
  • checkpoint_every (int, default 0): write checkpoint_<N>.pt every N epochs; 0 writes only best.pt.

TrainResult

What fit and resume return.

Attributes:

  • final_metrics (dict[str, dict[str, float]]): per target, the metrics on the held-out fold. A regression target reports mae, rmse, r2, smape (range 0 to 2) and band_10, band_25, band_50 (the share of plots within that relative band), in original units. A classification target reports accuracy, macro_f1, weighted_f1 and precision_<c>, recall_<c>, f1_<c> per class. A target with missing = Mask also reports n_labelled.
  • best_epoch (int): the epoch with the best held-out value of selection_metric.
  • train_loss_history, test_loss_history (list[float]): one entry per epoch; the second is empty when nothing is held out.
  • train_loss_history_by_target, test_loss_history_by_target (dict[str, list[float]]): those losses split into each target’s weighted term.
  • train_aux_loss_history (dict[str, list[float]]): the auxiliary terms of the training loss, moe and tabnet_sparsity.
  • lr_history (list[float]): the learning rate of each epoch’s last step.
  • selection_history (list[float]): the held-out value of selection_metric at each epoch.
  • baselines (dict[str, BaselineMetrics]): a naive baseline per target.
  • diagnostics (NetworkDiagnostics): the network’s state at the end of the fit.
  • train_time_seconds (float), effective_batch_size (int), resumed_from_epoch (int, 0 for a run trained from the start).

BaselineMetrics

A target’s naive baseline beside the model: baseline_mae, baseline_mse (predicting the training mean), model_mae, model_mse, skill_score (1 - model_mse / baseline_mse), r_squared, training_mean; for a classification target baseline_accuracy (predicting the most frequent training class), model_accuracy, accuracy_lift and training_mode. Regression values are in original units and match final_metrics.

CrossValidationResult

What cross_validate and cross_validate_spatial return: n_folds, mean_metrics and std_metrics (the mean and standard deviation of each metric across folds, by target), fold_results (one TrainResult per fold) and total_time_seconds.

SpatialBlockConfig

The blocks of cross_validate_spatial: lat_size and lon_size (float, default 1.0), the block height and width in degrees, and balance (bool, default False), which assigns blocks to folds by greedy bin-packing to even out the fold sizes instead of in turn.

ResidualAnalysis

What compute_residuals returns, in original units, over the held-out plots labelled for the target: target_name, predictions, actuals, residuals, test_rows (each row’s position in test_plot_ids()), mean_residual, std_residual, skewness, kurtosis and the residual quantiles q05, q25, q50, q75, q95.

ClassificationPredictions

What compute_classification_predictions returns, over the held-out plots labelled for the target: target_name, predicted_classes and actuals (int64 codes), probabilities ((n, n_classes)), test_rows (each row’s position in test_plot_ids()) and class_names (the labels in code order).

CalibrationResult

What compute_calibration returns: target_name, class_idx, bins (list[CalibrationBin]), expected_calibration_error and max_calibration_error. A classifier is calibrated when the plots it gives a probability p are right a share p of the time.

CalibrationBin

One bin of predicted probability: bin_start, bin_end, count (the plots in it), mean_predicted_prob and actual_frequency (the share of them predicted correctly).

NetworkDiagnostics

The activations of the species encoder’s hidden layers over the held-out fold: layers (list[LayerDiagnostics]), total_neurons, total_dead, total_saturated, overall_dead_fraction, overall_saturated_fraction, has_issues and summary, a sentence describing them.

LayerDiagnostics

One hidden layer: name, n_neurons, n_dead and dead_fraction (neurons that never activate), n_saturated and saturated_fraction, mean_activation, std_activation and sparsity.

PretrainConfig

The settings of JEPAPretrainer and SCARFPretrainer. Pretraining trains the encoder on a task built from the inputs alone, with no target, before the model is fitted.

  • Shared: pretrain_epochs (100), pretrain_lr (1e-4), pretrain_weight_decay (1e-4), batch_size (4096), batch_size_floor (1024), warmup_steps (0), device ("cpu"), vram_fraction (1.0) and seed (42), which seeds every draw the pretraining makes.
  • Masking, for JEPA: mask_ratio (0.3, the share of features masked) and mask_strategy (MaskStrategy, Random).
  • JEPA: ema_decay (0.996) and ema_decay_end (1.0), the decay of the slowly updated target encoder; predictor_hidden_dim (256), predictor_n_layers (2) and predictor_dropout (0.1).
  • SCARF: corruption_rate (0.6, the share of features replaced), temperature (0.1), projection_dim (128) and mixup_alpha (0.0), the strength of a mixup of the corrupted view with another plot of the batch; 0 switches it off.

JEPAPretrainer 

JEPAPretrainer(model, config=PretrainConfig())
pretrain(continuous, genus_ids=None, family_ids=None, ...)

Pretrains a model’s encoder in place by joint-embedding prediction (T-JEPA): the encoder reads a masked view of each plot and learns to predict the latent a slowly updated copy of itself gives the whole plot. pretrain takes the model inputs of ResolveModel.forward, continuous unstandardised and required, and returns a PretrainResult.

SCARFPretrainer 

SCARFPretrainer(model, config=PretrainConfig())
pretrain(continuous, genus_ids=None, family_ids=None, ...)

Pretrains a model’s encoder in place by contrastive learning (SCARF): each plot and a corrupted copy of it, with a share of its inputs replaced by values from other plots, form the pair the encoder learns to match. The inputs are those of JEPAPretrainer.pretrain.

pretrain_config = rc.PretrainConfig()
pretrain_config.pretrain_epochs = 5
fresh = rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, model.config)
scarf = rc.SCARFPretrainer(fresh, pretrain_config)
pretrained = scarf.pretrain(dataset.continuous_block(True), **inputs)
pretrained.loss_history

PretrainResult

What the JEPA, SCARF and masked-species pretrainers return: loss_history (one entry per epoch), epochs_completed, total_time_seconds and effective_batch_size.

MaskStrategy

Which features JEPA masks: Random (each feature on its own), Block (one contiguous range per plot) or Structured (whole contiguous groups of features).

MLMPretrainConfig

The settings of MaskedSpeciesPretrainer: mask_prob (0.15, the share of a plot’s species masked), pretrain_epochs (50), pretrain_lr (1e-4), pretrain_weight_decay (1e-4), batch_size (4096), batch_size_floor (1024), warmup_steps (0), device ("cpu"), vram_fraction (1.0) and seed (42).

MaskedSpeciesPretrainer 

MaskedSpeciesPretrainer(model, config=MLMPretrainConfig())
pretrain(*, species_ids, pool_mask, pool_genus_ids=None, pool_family_ids=None,
         pool_weights=None, ...)

Pretrains the species encoder of a Transformer-encoding model in place by masked-species prediction: a share of each plot’s species is hidden and the encoder learns to name them from the rest. pretrain takes the model inputs by keyword, species_ids and pool_mask required, and returns a PretrainResult.

transformer = rc.DatasetConfig()
transformer.species_encoding = rc.SpeciesEncodingMode.Transformer
tokens = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets, transformer)
token_model = rc.ResolveModel(
    tokens.schema, rc.model_config_for_dataset(tokens, rc.ModelConfig()))
masked = rc.MLMPretrainConfig()
masked.pretrain_epochs = 5
rc.MaskedSpeciesPretrainer(token_model, masked).pretrain(
    species_ids=tokens.species_ids, pool_mask=tokens.pool_mask,
    pool_genus_ids=tokens.pool_genus_ids,
    pool_family_ids=tokens.pool_family_ids,
    pool_weights=tokens.pool_weights)

VAEConfig

The settings of VAEPretrainer: latent_dim (64), encoder_dims ([512, 256, 128]), decoder_dims ([128, 256, 512]), dropout (0.1), kl_weight (1.0, the weight of the divergence term), kl_anneal_epochs (20, the epochs over which that weight rises from 0), pretrain_epochs (100), pretrain_lr (0.001), pretrain_weight_decay (0.01), batch_size (4096), batch_size_floor (1024), warmup_steps (0), device ("cpu"), vram_fraction (1.0) and seed (42).

VAEPretrainer 

VAEPretrainer(n_species, config=VAEConfig())
pretrain(species_vector)

A variational autoencoder, a network that compresses each plot’s species vector to latent_dim numbers and reconstructs it, trained on the plots alone. n_species is the vocabulary size (ResolveSchema.n_species_vocab); pretrain reads the sparse encoding’s species_vector and returns a VAEPretrainResult. get_latent_dim() returns the latent width and get_projection_weights() the encoder’s first layer, one row per unit of its first hidden layer and one column per species.

sparse = rc.DatasetConfig()
sparse.species_encoding = rc.SpeciesEncodingMode.Sparse
vectors = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets, sparse)
vae_config = rc.VAEConfig()
vae_config.latent_dim = 8
vae_config.pretrain_epochs = 20
vae = rc.VAEPretrainer(vectors.schema.n_species_vocab, vae_config)
vae.pretrain(vectors.species_vector).loss_history[-1]

VAEPretrainResult

What VAEPretrainer.pretrain returns: loss_history, recon_loss_history and kl_loss_history (one entry per epoch), epochs_completed, total_time_seconds and effective_batch_size.

LossConfigMode

The regression loss: MAE (mean absolute error alone), SMAPE (symmetric mean absolute percentage error), Combined (the three phases of phase_boundaries, the default) or NCA (Combined, with a neighbourhood components analysis term added for every classification target).

LRSchedulerType

How the learning rate changes over a run: None_ (constant), StepLR (times lr_gamma every lr_step_size epochs), CosineAnnealing (down to lr_min), ReduceOnPlateau (times lr_plateau_factor when the held-out value stalls) or LinearDecay (down to lr_min in a straight line, step by step).

SelectionMetric

The held-out value a run selects by: Loss (the lowest wins) or Accuracy (the highest held-out accuracy of the one classification target; refused without a held-out fold or without exactly one classification target).

ActivationType

ReLU, LeakyReLU, GELU, SiLU, Tanh, Mish, ELU, SELU, Softplus or PReLU.

NormLayerType

BatchNorm, LayerNorm, GroupNorm, RMSNorm or None_.

EncoderArchitecture

The shared encoder: MLP, FTTransformer, TabNet, SAINT, TraitNet, GNN, ExcelFormer or HeterogeneousGNN.

MoERoutingType

How a mixture of experts routes a plot: None_ (no mixture), Soft (every expert, weighted) or TopK (the moe_top_k highest-weighted experts).

MoEPlacement

Where the mixture sits. Under Tail the experts are the encoder’s final stage: hidden_dims without its last two widths is the backbone, and the mixture maps it to hidden_dims[-1], the latent. It is available to every species encoding of the MLP encoder. Under Post the encoder makes its latent as usual and the mixture maps it to one of the same width; any architecture takes it.

GNNType

The graph layer of EncoderArchitecture.GNN: GCN, GAT or GraphSAGE.

GraphConstructionMode

What the plot graph of EncoderArchitecture.GNN measures neighbourhood on: Spatial (the coordinates), Taxonomic (the genus and family slots) or CoOccurrence (the species vector).

TraitInteractionMode

How TraitNet combines the environment and a species’ traits: Bilinear, MLP or Attention.

TabMAggregation

How TabM combines its ensemble: Mean or Median.

TransformerPooling

How the transformer encoding pools its species tokens into one vector: Attention or Cls (a learned summary token, which needs at least one attention layer).

ParallelAggregation

How a parallel block combines its branches: Concat, Sum, Mean, Attention or Gated.
